History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with a PMH significant for 
diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement also 
complicated by bowel fistula and perforation s/p colostomy, 
CVID, DMII who presents for her third dose of high dose 
methotrexate.
.
Today she feels well. She has had some weakness at home, likely 
deconditioning (its equal and bilateral) and some continued pain 
from mucositis. She has been eating well. She denies any fever 
or chills, abdominal pain. She has had good output from her 
ostomy. She also denies any blurry vision, or focal weakness.
.
Of note she was recently discharged after a long admission for 
an SBO, during which time she was found to have CNS involvement 
of her lymphoma, proven on biopsy, and treated with high dose 
methotrexate and R-CHOP. Her course was complicated by severe 
mucositis. She was discharged home for the holidays.
.  
.

(-) Denies fever, chills, night sweats, recent weight loss or 
gain. Denies headache. Denied cough, shortness of breath. Denied 
chest pain or palpitations. Denied nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, 
constipation or abdominal pain. Denied arthralgias or myalgias. 
All other review of systems are negative.

-___: bronchoscopy with BAL + for staph aureus and yeast.

small bowel with fistulas between small and large bowel and 
focal perforation in the area involved by necrotic tumor. In 
areas, the bowel wall was completely replaced by necrotic tumor. 
The tumor was nearly totally necrotic in the sections examined. 
Margins of resection were free of necrosis and tumor. There was 
no evidence of large cell lymphoma in the mesenteric lymph nodes 
examined.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old with diffuse large b-cell lymphoma, CVID, and DM2 
admitted for high dose methotrexate.

#  Lymphoma: She has CNS involvement proven on biopsy during 
last admission, with good interval response to high dose 
methotrexate.  She has had symptomatic improvement of her 
weakness and her mucositis. She received MTX at 3.5g/m2 and 
tolerated the treatment well. She cleared the MTX in 48 hours. 
The patient was scheduled to return for admission for high-dose 
MTX on ___. Dexamethasone was decreased to 1 mg bid from 2 
mg bid. 

#  Abdominal pain: Day 4 of MTX treatment she began having 
increased abdominal pain and a tremendous amount of gas.  Given 
her history of perforation she was sent for a KUB which showed 
no obstruction or free air. She continued to have abdominal pain 
on HD#7 and her diet was changed to clear liquids, which she 
tolerated. Stool studies were sent and ___ C.diff toxin returned 
positive. PO Vancomycin was started to complete a 14-day course. 
CT abd was significant for small bowel wall thickening - likely 
c/w infection. On discharge, the patient's stool output was 
almost at baseline and abdominal pain had resolved. 
.  
#  DM2: On metformin at home her blood sugars are reportedly 
well controlled between 80-160 on 500mg BID of metformin. While 
in the hospital her BG ranged as high as 497 and was regularly 
elevated between 240-320. We started her on lantus and increased 
it to 12 units. Her sliding scale was aggressively uptitrated. 
She admittedly would not adhere to diabetic diet which she was 
written for (she would eat over 10 packs ___ crackers for 
a snack).  She told us her sugars were better controlled at home 
because she is more careful with her diet. She was not 
discharged on insulin out of concern for low bs. A1C was 
added-on and was pending at the time of discharge. That patient 
may require insulin in the future. 

#  CVID: She recieves IVIg every three weeks. Prior to admission 
she last recieved treatment on ___.  She was given a dose of 
40g IVIg on ___ with pretreatment with tylenol and 
benadryl.
  
#  Pain: She has chronic pain issues in her back and gets pain 
oxycodone at home. Continued her outpatient pain meds.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,
It was a pleasure taking part in your care.

You were admitted to ___ for high dose methotrexate to treat

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST ON ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with B-cell lymphoma, here to start high-dose
methotrexate.  Evaluate for pleural effusions.

IMPRESSION:  PA and lateral chest compared to ___:

Lungs are fully expanded and clear.  Previous mediastinal vascular engorgement
has resolved.  Heart size is normal.  There is no pleural effusion or good
evidence for central adenopathy.  A right subclavian infusion port catheter
ends in the region of the superior cavoatrial junction.  No pneumothorax.

STUDY:  Abdomen supine and erect films, ___.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with history of bowel perforation in the setting
of chemotherapy now with increasing abdominal pain.  Status post methotrexate
treatment. Evaluate for free air.

FINDINGS:  There is no free intra-abdominal gas.  The bowel gas pattern is
nonspecific with air and stool seen throughout non-dilated loops of colon and
few loops of small bowel.  Hardware is seen within the lower lumbar spine. 
There are some degenerative changes of bilateral hips.

IMPRESSION:

Nonspecific bowel gas pattern without obstruction or free intra-abdominal air.

CLINICAL HISTORY: Intermittent crampy abdominal pain, history of bowel
perforation status post colostomy.

COMPARISON:  CXR ___, CT ___.

FINDINGS:  Supine and erect views of the abdomen were obtained.  The bowel gas
pattern is nonspecific with air within non-dilated loops small and large
bowel.  There is no evidence of ascites, pneumatosis, or free intra-peritoneal
air.  The splenic silhouette is enlarged.  Suture chain material is seen in
the left lower quadrant.  Spinal hardware is in place.  Degenerative changes
are noted in the hips bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:  Nonspecific bowel gas pattern without obstruction or free
intra-peritoneal air.

ADDENDUM:  There is retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy in the left paraaortic
region.  This measures 1.2 x 1.3 cm on the axial images and a conglomerate of
these nodes measures 8.0 cm in length.  On the most recent scan from
___, this is stable in size measuring 1.1 x 1.3 cm in cross section and
7.7 cm in length on the coronal images.

INDICATION:  ___ female with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma on
chemotherapy, suspected Crohn's with small bowel-colosigmoid fistula post
small bowel resection x2, resection of descending colon and sigmoid, and
colostomy.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the
greater trochanters with intravenous and oral contrast.  Coronal and sagittal
multiplanar reformations were generated.

FINDINGS:  The visualized heart and lung bases are clear.  There are no
pleural or pericardial effusions.  A small sliding hiatal hernia is present.

ABDOMEN:  The liver enhances homogeneously without focal lesions.  The
gallbladder is partially distended without wall edema, stones, sludge, or
pericholecystic fluid.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary
dilatation.  The pancreas is slightly atrophic.  The spleen is enlarged,
measuring 16.3 cm.

The adrenals are normal.  The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast promptly
and symmetrically, without masses or hydronephrosis.

PELVIS:  The bladder is distended with urine, and right ureteral jet is
visualized.  Mild apparent wall thickening may be secondary to
underdistension.  The uterus and ovaries are surgically absent, with intact
vaginal cuff.

GASTROINTESTINAL:  The stomach and duodenum are normal.  Changes of small
bowel resection are noted, with suture lines in the mid abdomen (2B:48) and
mid pelvis (2B:60).  These are located in the jejunum and ileum, respectively.
Just distal to the jejunal anastomosis site, there is diffuse moderate
submucosal bowel wall edema extending over approximately 15 cm length.  This
is represented by "target sign," with submucosal hypodensity and a normal
mucosal and serosal enhancement.  The jejunal loop is focally dilated to 4 cm.
Just distal to this, there is focal dilation of jejunum to 5 cm, with
normalization of wall thickness.  Multiple prominent loops of distal jejunum
and ileum measure up to 3 cm, with scattered air-fluid levels.  There has been
interval development of pneumatosis within multiple loops of ileum in the
pelvis.  

The ascending and transverse colon are partially decompressed, but appear
normal.  Colostomy exits through the left mid abdomen, without evidence of
leak or obstruction.  The descending and sigmoid colon are surgically absent.
___ pouch in the posterior pelvis is normal, with multiple fluid-filled
loops and suture line along the left pelvic side wall.

Additional locules of extraluminal air are seen in the retroperitoneum along
the right paracolic gutter, and in the anterior pelvis adjacent to multiple
ileal loops.  There is no portal or mesenteric venous gas to suggest ischemia.

Scattered calcifications and soft plaques are noted in the abdominal aorta and
iliac arteries, with patent branch vessels.  Multiple prominent intra-
abdominal lymph nodes are present, measuring up to 5-6 mm in the mesentery, 7
mm in the left paraaortic region.  A large retroperitoneal lymph node
conglomerate measure 9.3 x 1.3 cm in the left paraortic region (___)
and 3.7 x 0.7 cm in the right paraortic region (300B:19). Multiple additional
prominent nodes are present, likely reactive.  There is trace mesenteric
stranding and edema throughout the mesentery, indicating acute inflammation.

The bones are diffusely demineralized.  There is straightening of the lumbar
lordosis.  Changes of L4-5 laminectomy and posterior fusion are present.  The
tip of the L5 pedicle screw is again noted to extend anteriorly just beyond
the anterior margins of the vertebra, but there is no evidence of fat
stranding, and no adjacent viscera.  There is a 1.3 cm well-defined sclerotic
lesion in the right posterior acetabulum, likely a bone island.  A 1.7 x 1.2
cm well circumscribed, lytic lesion in the right ilium may represent fibrous
dysplasia.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Interval development of submucosal jejunal wall edema distal to
anastomosis, pneumatosis in multiple ileal loops, and trace locules of
extraluminal air in the anterior pelvis and retroperitoneum.  Given the
interval development of changes within a two-week period, this is consistent
with infectious or inflammatory changes, ischemia is also in the differential
diagnosis.
2.  Intact ileal anastomosis and colostomy, and ___ pouch in the left
abdomen.
3.  Stable splenomegaly.

Initial findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ on ___ at
11:40 p.m.  Final results were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ ___ at
12:00 p.m.
